note: M136 evidence for public-derive-from-behavior-v6 (G17 phase 2): 24 upstream TypeScript functions over one array parameter from 21 MIT / Apache-2.0 / ISC repos, run on examples whose numbers include NaN, Infinity and -Infinity. Two sets. (a) v4-upstream: the 20 of M113's 28 upstream functions that read a number (the other 8 read only strings or booleans, so no v6 task can be written for them), same commit, path, file sha256 and license as in m113-derive-list-evidence.json. (b) non-finite-upstream: 4 new functions found by GitHub code search for exported one-expression functions over an array parameter that call Number.isFinite / isFinite / isNaN (3,761 distinct files from 24 searches fetched at their default branch and screened; 40 matches outside BigNumber helpers sat in an exported declaration; after dropping nested local helpers, bodies or types outside v6 (sort, Set, map to a computed value, BigNumber strings, nested arrays) and repos without a MIT / Apache-2.0 / ISC license (unlicensed or AGPL), 4 remain; each is then pinned to the repo's HEAD commit at fetch time). zkwokleung/chart-quest compact takes (number | null)[]; it is typed number[] here, which drops the null case as M113 drops optional fields. Examples are the upstream function run on a seeded grid (seed 136, 48 rows of lists of length 0-6; numbers from -150..150 plus NaN, Infinity and -Infinity; strings from M113's per-field literals). The first 6 rows train, extended only by PeaceAI's own refusals the way an issue author would (as M113; an asked row is answered by the upstream function), at most 40 rows. Every training slice holds a non-finite value. Held out: the other grid rows plus every v6 probe list not in the training rows. Results: 14 derive and are right on every held-out row (3565 rows, 1799 of them with a non-finite value, 0 wrong): sum (7), sum of kept (3), filter (1), filter Number.isFinite (2), some !Number.isFinite (1). 5 derive a max / min program that fits every example but is WRONG on 11 held-out rows each (wrongOnNaN): the upstream bodies use Math.max(...xs) / Math.min(...xs), which give NaN when a list holds NaN, while v6's max / min program skips NaN; no training row showed a NaN in a non-empty list, and no v6 gate or probe asked for one, because no rival program in the DSL propagates NaN. 5 are refused: runtimeTotal (`movie.runtime || 0` maps NaN to 0, outside the DSL) derive_no_fit; maxNumber and max (`Math.max(max, value)` seeded with 0, NaN-propagating) derive_no_fit; hasError (`errorCount > 0`) derive_ambiguous after 40 rows, though v4 derives it on integers; calcActiveSum (outOfVocabulary: a kept-by-flag sum that also skips non-finite credits, two conditions) derive_no_fit. The rule's evidence block counts the 14 functions that derive with 0 wrong (14 repos). Examples are stored as issue lines (`ARGS gives OUT`, read back by lexListValues with the v6 flag) since JSON has no NaN. The evidence test re-derives each entry from its recorded lines; no third-party code is run by the test.
